title: Grade 4 ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — 5.1.1 Virtues: Kindness to Allah’s Creatures

pages.lesson:
PAGE 1: Overview

OVERVIEW
========

Allah (S.W.T.) created people, animals, birds, insects, fish and plants. Islam teaches Muslims to be kind to all of them. In this sub-strand you will name Allah’s creatures around you, learn why kindness to them matters, and practise caring for them, including animals that carry people and loads, as an act of ibadah.

## Strand 5.0: Akhlaq (Moral Teachings)
Sub-strand 5.1.1: Virtues: Kindness to Allah’s Creatures
Suggested lessons: 2

## Learning outcomes
By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to:
a) assess the significance of showing kindness to Allah’s creatures in the environment
b) demonstrate ways of showing kindness to Allah’s creatures as an act of ibadah
c) appreciate Allah’s creatures by being kind to them

## Key inquiry questions
1. What are some of Allah’s creatures in your environment?
2. Why should you be kind to Allah’s creatures?
3. How can you be kind to Allah’s creatures?

## Core competencies
• Learning to Learn: the skill of working collaboratively is enhanced as learners discuss the significance of being kind to Allah’s creatures.
• Communication and collaboration: the skill of speaking and writing is enhanced as learners discuss the significance of being kind to Allah’s creatures, in pairs/groups, write the points in their notebook.
• Creativity and imagination: the skill of networking is enhanced as learners dramatise ways of showing kindness to Allah’s creatures.

## Values
• Social justice: responsibility enhanced as learners dramatise ways of showing kindness to Allah’s creatures.
• Responsibility: accountability enhanced as learners watch on digital devices/charts/photos appropriate ways of caring for Allah’s creatures
• Respect: enhanced as learners respect each other’s view when discussing the significance of being kind to Allah’s creatures, in pairs/groups

## Pertinent and contemporary issues
• Socio-economic issues: Animal welfare education as learners dramatise ways of showing kindness to Allah’s creatures.

## Links to other learning areas
• Agriculture as learners care for animals.

## Source
• KICD Grade 4 Islamic Religious Education Curriculum Design (Revised 2024) — Strand 5.0 Akhlaq (Moral Teachings), Sub-strand 5.1.1 Virtues: Kindness to Allah’s Creatures
• Qur’an 16:8
• Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim: Hadith of the thirsty dog, the cat, mercy and planting trees; Sunan Abu Dawud: Hadith on animals that cannot speak

PAGE 2: Lesson 1: Allah’s creatures around us and why we should be kind to them

LESSON 1: ALLAH’S CREATURES AROUND US AND WHY WE SHOULD BE KIND TO THEM
============================================================

## What you will learn
• Name creatures of Allah (S.W.T.) found in your environment.
• Give reasons why Muslims should be kind to Allah’s creatures.
• Tell the Hadith of the man who gave water to a thirsty dog.

Curriculum outcomes: a) assess the significance of showing kindness to Allah’s creatures in the environment; c) appreciate Allah’s creatures by being kind to them

## Introduction
Look around your home and school. You may see goats, chickens, cats, birds on a tree, ants on the ground and flowers in the garden. Every one of them was created by Allah (S.W.T.), and every one of them needs care.

## Notes
### Allah’s creatures in our environment
Allah (S.W.T.) is the Creator of everything. His creatures around us include:

- Animals: cows, goats, sheep, donkeys, camels, cats and dogs
- Birds: chickens, ducks, doves and weaver birds
- Insects: bees, butterflies and ants
- Fish and other water creatures in rivers, lakes and the ocean
- Plants: trees, grass, flowers and crops such as maize and beans

All these creatures feel hunger and thirst or need water and sunlight to live. Allah made them, and He has made people responsible for looking after the earth.

### Why we should be kind to Allah’s creatures
- Kindness pleases Allah and earns rewards. The Prophet (S.A.W) told of a man who found a dog panting and licking mud because of thirst. The man went down into a well, filled his leather sock with water and gave the dog a drink. Allah thanked him and forgave his sins. The companions asked whether there is a reward for being kind to animals. The Prophet (S.A.W) said there is a reward for kindness to every living creature (Bukhari and Muslim).
- Cruelty angers Allah. The Prophet (S.A.W) told of a woman who was punished because she locked up a cat. She did not feed it, and she did not let it go to find food for itself (Bukhari and Muslim).
- The Prophet (S.A.W) said that whoever does not show mercy will not be shown mercy (Bukhari and Muslim).
- Animals and plants help us. They give us milk, meat, eggs, honey, food, shade, clean air and transport. Caring for them is a way of thanking Allah.
- Planting is charity. The Prophet (S.A.W) taught that when a Muslim plants a tree or a crop and a bird, a person or an animal eats from it, it is counted as charity for him (Bukhari and Muslim).

### Showing appreciation
We appreciate Allah’s creatures when we do not hurt them for fun, do not destroy plants without reason and feel thankful to Allah for them.

## Key words
• creature — anything that Allah (S.W.T.) has created and that has life, such as a person, an animal or a plant
• kindness — being gentle, caring and helpful
• mercy (rahma) — showing pity and care to others who need it

## Worked examples

### Example 1
Juma sees a bird with a broken wing near the school gate. What would a kind Muslim learner do?

Working:
1. Remember that the bird is a creature of Allah and can feel pain.
2. Do not throw stones or play with it.
3. Tell a teacher or an adult who can help it and give it water.

Answer: Protect the bird, give it water and get an adult to help it.

## Activity: Creatures of Allah in our environment
You will need: Exercise book, Pencil, Pictures or charts of animals, insects, fish and plants
1. In groups, walk around the school compound with your teacher.
2. List the creatures of Allah (S.W.T.) you see under the headings animals, birds, insects, fish and plants.
3. Back in class, discuss why we should be kind to each creature on your list.
4. Write three reasons in your notebook and share them with the class.

## Practice
1. Name four creatures of Allah (S.W.T.) found at your home or school.
2. What did the man in the Hadith do for the thirsty dog, and what was his reward?
3. Why was the woman in the Hadith of the cat punished?
4. Give two reasons why Muslims should be kind to Allah’s creatures.

## Summary
• People, animals, birds, insects, fish and plants are all creatures of Allah (S.W.T.).
• Kindness to creatures earns rewards; cruelty is punished.
• Whoever does not show mercy will not be shown mercy.

### Answers to practice
1. Any four, for example goat, chicken, cat, bee, ant, tree, grass or fish.
2. He filled his leather sock with water from a well and gave the dog a drink. Allah forgave his sins.
3. She locked up the cat, did not feed it and did not let it go to find its own food.
4. Any two: kindness earns rewards from Allah; cruelty is a sin; the Prophet (S.A.W) taught mercy; animals and plants help us; caring for them is thanking Allah.

PAGE 3: Lesson 2: Caring for animals and plants as an act of ibadah

LESSON 2: CARING FOR ANIMALS AND PLANTS AS AN ACT OF IBADAH
===========================================================

## What you will learn
• Identify domestic animals used for transport.
• Explain how animals can be used safely for transport.
• Show ways of caring for animals, insects, plants and fish.

Curriculum outcomes: b) demonstrate ways of showing kindness to Allah’s creatures as an act of ibadah; c) appreciate Allah’s creatures by being kind to them

## Introduction
In many parts of Kenya a donkey pulls a cart of water, a camel carries goods, or oxen pull a cart full of harvest. These animals work hard for people. How should they be treated?

## Notes
### Domestic animals used for transport
The Qur’an reminds us that Allah created horses, mules and donkeys for people to ride and as adornment (Qur’an 16:8). In Kenya, domestic animals used for transport include:

- Donkeys, which carry water, firewood and farm produce or pull carts
- Camels, which carry people and goods in dry areas
- Oxen, which pull ox-carts and ploughs
- Horses, which people ride

### Using transport animals safely and kindly
- Do not load an animal with more than it can carry.
- Give it enough food, water and rest, especially on a hot day.
- Do not beat it, poke it with sharp sticks or shout at it.
- Keep carts, saddles and ropes in good condition so they do not cut the animal’s skin.
- Treat wounds and take a sick animal to an animal doctor (veterinary officer).
- Do not work a sick, very young or pregnant animal too hard.

The Prophet (S.A.W) warned people to fear Allah concerning animals that cannot speak, to ride them when they are fit and to look after them well (Abu Dawud).

### Other ways of showing kindness
- Animals and birds: feed and give water to pets and livestock, give them clean shelter, and do not throw stones at birds or keep them in cages without care.
- Insects: do not kill bees and butterflies for fun; they help flowers to make fruit.
- Plants: water seedlings, plant trees and do not cut or break trees without a good reason.
- Fish: do not throw rubbish or chemicals into rivers, lakes and the ocean.

### Kindness as ibadah
Ibadah means any act done to please Allah. When a Muslim waters a plant, feeds a hungry cat or gives a donkey rest with the intention (niyyah) of pleasing Allah, that good deed is ibadah and earns reward.

## Key words
• domestic animal — an animal kept by people at home or on the farm
• ibadah — worship; any good act done to please Allah (S.W.T.)
• niyyah — intention in the heart when doing an act

## Worked examples

### Example 1
A boy loads a donkey with six full jerrycans of water on a hot afternoon and beats it when it walks slowly. What is wrong, and what should he do?

Working:
1. The load is too heavy for the donkey.
2. Beating the animal is cruel and displeases Allah.
3. He should reduce the load, let the donkey rest and give it water.

Answer: He is overloading and beating the donkey. He should carry a lighter load, rest it, give it water and never beat it.

## Activity: Drama: A kind owner
You will need: Pictures or video of donkeys, camels, oxen and horses, Simple props such as a rope and a container of water
1. Watch pictures or a video clip showing good ways of caring for animals, insects, plants and fish.
2. In groups, name the domestic animals used for transport in your area.
3. Prepare a short play: one learner is a cruel owner of a donkey, and another learner teaches him how to treat the donkey kindly.
4. Present the play and let the class say which acts of kindness they saw.

## Practice
1. Name three domestic animals used for transport in Kenya.
2. Give three ways of using a donkey safely for transport.
3. How can watering a young tree become an act of ibadah?
4. State one way of being kind to fish.

## Summary
• Donkeys, camels, oxen and horses help people to carry loads and travel.
• Transport animals need food, water, rest, fair loads and gentle handling.
• Caring for creatures with the intention of pleasing Allah is ibadah.

### Answers to practice
1. Any three: donkey, camel, ox, horse.
2. Any three: do not overload it; give it food, water and rest; do not beat it; keep the cart and ropes in good condition; treat its wounds.
3. When it is done with the intention of pleasing Allah (S.W.T.).
4. Do not throw rubbish or chemicals into rivers, lakes or the ocean.
pages.quiz:
REVISION QUIZ — 5.1.1 VIRTUES: KINDNESS TO ALLAH’S CREATURES
========================================

Answer all the questions, then mark yourself on the Answers tab.

1. Which of these is NOT a creature of Allah (S.W.T.)?
   A. A bee
   B. A mango tree
   C. A plastic bag
   D. A fish

2. In the Hadith, why did Allah forgive the man who met a thirsty dog?
   A. He chased the dog away
   B. He gave the dog water to drink
   C. He sold the dog
   D. He built a house for the dog

3. Why was a woman punished because of a cat?
   A. She fed it too much
   B. She locked it up without food
   C. She gave it away
   D. She bathed it

4. Complete the teaching of the Prophet (S.A.W): Whoever does not show mercy …

5. Which animal is commonly used to carry goods in the dry areas of Kenya?
   A. Camel
   B. Cat
   C. Goat
   D. Chicken

6. Which of these is a safe way to use a donkey for transport?
   A. Loading it until it falls
   B. Giving it water and rest
   C. Beating it to walk faster
   D. Working it when it is sick

7. What does the word ibadah mean?

8. According to the Prophet (S.A.W), what is a Muslim’s reward when a bird eats from a tree he planted?
   A. Nothing
   B. It is counted as charity for him
   C. He must pay a fine
   D. He must cut the tree

9. Amina sees boys throwing stones at birds. What should she do?
   A. Join them
   B. Laugh at the birds
   C. Tell them kindly to stop and inform an adult
   D. Walk away and say nothing ever

10. Give two ways of showing kindness to plants.
pages.answers:
ANSWERS — 5.1.1 VIRTUES: KINDNESS TO ALLAH’S CREATURES
========================================

1. C. A plastic bag
   A plastic bag is made by people. Bees, trees and fish are living creatures created by Allah.

2. B. He gave the dog water to drink
   He filled his leather sock with water from the well and gave the thirsty dog a drink.

3. B. She locked it up without food
   She locked up the cat, neither feeding it nor letting it find food.

4. … will not be shown mercy.
   This Hadith is reported by Bukhari and Muslim.

5. A. Camel
   Camels can walk long distances with little water and carry people and goods.

6. B. Giving it water and rest
   A working animal needs food, water and rest.

7. Worship, or any good act done to please Allah (S.W.T.).
   Even kindness to animals is ibadah when done to please Allah.

8. B. It is counted as charity for him
   Whatever a person, bird or animal eats from what a Muslim plants is charity for him.

9. C. Tell them kindly to stop and inform an adult
   Birds are Allah’s creatures. Stopping cruelty is part of kindness.

10. Any two: water them, plant trees, do not break or cut trees without reason, protect seedlings.
   Plants are living creatures of Allah that give us food, shade and clean air.
